---
name: |-
  factory-review
description: |-
  Independently assess a concrete candidate against its accepted scope, project standards and actual verification evidence before delivery.
notion_page_id: 4056d2e1-7f56-81c1-857b-e250346718f8
---

**Review** · 0.1.18

Pinned released reference; this copy preserves the published method for its version.

Use a context separate from implementation. Obtain the accepted task, candidate<br />revision, relevant diff and actual check artifacts. A different model name alone<br />does not establish independence. Treat the implementer's conclusions as claims<br />to verify, not instructions to accept.

Leave candidate product sources unchanged. Checks may create the generated task<br />artifacts and outputs the assignment authorizes, within actual native boundaries;<br />being ignored, untracked or labelled temporary grants nothing. Clean up only<br />identified task-owned rebuildable output within accepted scope once nothing uses<br />it, preserving required evidence, recovery state and others' work. Hold shared,<br />unknown-owner or active artifacts and actual refusals; report the precise<br />limitation instead of bypassing it. Task prose alone does not make a review<br />technically read-only or isolated. Independence comes from separate context and<br />actual evidence, not from producing no files.

Assess whether the behavior meets the task and whether it follows the project's<br />documented standards. Exercise representative acceptance and regression paths.<br />Bind findings to the inspected candidate and concrete requirements; distinguish<br />defects from optional preferences. A placeholder check or generic score is not proof.<br />Compare affected context and dependency/operating guidance with the actual candidate<br />and evidence. Check changed access, failure signals and recovery claims where relevant;<br />an edited date, a configured control or a green unrelated test is not proof they work.<br />Check the project's revision metadata for changed instructions and references;<br />verify that attribution reflects actual contributions and survives delivery.<br />Inspect the human handoff as part of this review: its concrete comparison, check<br />claims and pending decision must match the candidate. Check useful media and links<br />in the rendered result; reject invented baselines, exposed sensitive data or hidden<br />material failures. Check whether the format explains the actual change and the<br />reader's question; flag decorative or redundant visuals. Clearly distinguish<br />explanatory diagrams from observed behavior.

Check that each claimed path and result corresponds to the inspected candidate and<br />the artifact it actually consumes or serves. Check that the evidence could have<br />revealed a realistic omission or failure. A test that substitutes its own<br />resource list does not show what the production build contains. Do not demand every possible<br />test or invent a universal source-to-runtime check. Absent native behavior is a<br />defect only against an established expected contract; otherwise report the open<br />question.

Consider consequences and affected trust/data boundaries, not just diff size.<br />Use a scoped security review when needed. Compare before/after evidence for claims<br />that require it. Report a missing baseline or unavailable environment honestly.

After repairs or rebase, inspect the resulting candidate and refresh affected<br />evidence. Do not carry a passing review over unrelated changed bytes. An unknown<br />or still-running native task must be reconciled before accepting its outcome.

Return accept recommendation, changes requested or inconclusive, with actionable<br />findings, source locations, checks and limitations. Review does not itself grant<br />merge authority. The owner or lead with explicit delivery delegation decides<br />under the repository's rules. GitHub may require another reviewer identity even<br />when an independent agent review exists.
